title: Keep the editor's Open Recent menu in order

blocks.text: The editor's **Open Recent** menu has three bug reports. A file the user opens again stays where it was in the list instead of coming to the top. On a fresh install, the editor crashes at startup while looking for a file to reopen. And once the menu is full, the file the user has just opened is the one that disappears.
`RecentFiles` keeps the paths in a `LinkedHashSet`, oldest first, and `menu()` already shows them most recent first. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/RecentFiles.java`:

items: `open(path)`: the opened file becomes the most recent one, and the menu holds at most `capacity` files;
`mostRecent()`: the file to reopen on startup, or an empty `Optional` when there is none.

cases.says: files opened one after another appear most recent first, and the last one opened is the one to reopen
opening a file that is already in the menu moves it to the top, without a duplicate
with no file opened yet, there is nothing to reopen, and asking does not throw
when the menu is full, opening another file drops the one opened longest ago, not the new one

origin.section: On LinkedHashSet and LinkedHashMap, addFirst and putLast Move an Existing Entry

concepts: On a LinkedHashSet or LinkedHashMap, addFirst/addLast and putFirst/putLast move an existing entry, while add and put leave it where it was.
getFirst() and getLast() throw NoSuchElementException on an empty collection, while firstEntry() on an empty map returns null, so code moved from get(0) changes its exception.
